note: SECTION w3 (1:00–1:30), THE NEGATIVE IN PITCH. LISTEN FOR 1:11.9–1:25.6, six cells of 'where it was' after the three on the wiw-negative card. The tune takes four of the scale's seven notes; the three it leaves out lie one between each pair it steps across: D flat between E flat and C, B flat between C and A flat, G between A flat and F. Every stroke of the negative sat on low F. Now each gap takes the note between the two missing notes around it: two D flats, three B flats, one G, and F where nothing lies between. So the strokes come down the scale and the holes are the steps they skip: you can sing the missing note into each one. Two cells at a time: the bass alone under both guitars' F (1:11.9), the left guitar with it (1:16.5), then both (1:21.0). The last of those is the cell where the snare says the four holes, so drum and strings between them say the whole scale in turn; then the cell with no band, as before; then the negative is on F again for the bass to start the tune from in the quiet middle. 72 notes change pitch (36 bass, 24 left, 12 right); no note moves, none is added or removed; kit untouched. MEASURED: the bass alone reads D flat 2, B flat 1, G1, F1 in all six cells; the left guitar's muted strokes read within 3 percent of those in its four; the right guitar's did not give a clean reading (muted, through the amp), so how clearly the guitars speak the line is for an ear. The bass is 1.7 dB louder on the higher notes and the six cells 0.2 to 0.4 dB louder mastered. Against the eleven records the six cells go from about 2 dB under to level at 60-120 Hz; 250-500 Hz stays 2.8 over. (1) THE TUNE IS MADE WHOLE. In the three cells before the handover each of those three notes becomes a fifth as well, one more a cell, in the order they will go: C at 0:31.2, A flat too at 0:34.4, F too at 0:37.1. The last cell is the whole tune in fifths, which the song otherwise keeps for its slow last statement at 3:22; the next thing heard is the crash, the ring's E flat and no band. Both guitars gain only the upper note of six fifths each; no note moves; the bass is as written.
(2) THE TWO CLOCKS CLOSE. The tune is eleven ticks long and the bar twelve, so its first note falls one tick nearer the bar line every cell: three ticks after it at 0:30, two, one, and on it at 0:37.5, which is why the form turns there. The drummer plants those three bar lines on the floor tom (0:30.0, 0:32.5, 0:35.0, each harder), as he planted the opening's (0:02.5-0:10), with the foot (two new kick strokes; at 0:32.5 the tune's own F already has it).
